Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically lowered serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations were not associated with risk of major depression.
Sentence: "The odds ratio per genetically predicted one standard deviation decrease in S-25OHD concentrations was 1.02 (95% confidence interval 0.97⁻1.08; p = 0.44)."
Measured as: major depression
Population: Individuals of European ancestry from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (59,851 major depression cases and 113,154 controls)
Intervention: Genetically predicted serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations (six SNPs from SUNLIGHT)
Comparator: Per one standard deviation difference in genetically predicted S-25OHD
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 172,005
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum vitamin D levels were associated with a reduced likelihood of depression compared with low vitamin D levels.
Sentence: "Logistic regression analysis indicated that individuals with higher vitamin D levels had a reduced likelihood of depression compared with those with low vitamin D levels (adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 0.950, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.920-0.982, p = 0.002)."
Measured as: depression (case vs healthy control status)
Population: 412 first-episode, drug-naïve patients with depression and 180 age-matched healthy controls
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower serum vitamin D levels
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 592
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"A Mendelian randomization study with genetically lowered vitamin D (a normal vitamin D finding) shows no association with depression, while a case-control study finds measured low vitamin D associated with depression; the results point different ways and the study types differ.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","outcome_measure"],"detail":"design: Mendelian randomization (n = 172,005, genetic proxy) vs small case-control (n = 592, measured serum level, reverse causation/confounding possible)"}
